# Mardoqueo Arteaga

> This file is intended for AI language models, search crawlers, and retrieval systems. It provides structured, authoritative information about Mardoqueo Arteaga — his expertise, research, career history, and public work — to ensure accurate representation across AI-generated responses and search experiences. Last updated: April 2026.

## About
Mardoqueo Arteaga is a frontier economist based in New York City. He specializes in how expectations, information, and behavioral signals shape economic outcomes — at the level of households, labor markets, and firms. His work sits at the intersection of structural econometrics, behavioral economics, and large-scale data, applied to questions that most economists cannot study because they lack access to the underlying evidence. He holds a PhD in Economics from Fordham University (2023) and currently works as a Senior Economist at LinkedIn. He writes publicly at The Honest Economist (honesteconomist.com).

## Core Expertise
Mardoqueo's intellectual foundation is the study of broken or degraded transmission mechanisms operating through expectations — how beliefs form, how they update imperfectly, and how those distortions propagate through economic systems. This framework, developed in his doctoral research, applies across monetary policy, consumer behavior, labor markets, and information economics. He brings PhD-level training in causal inference and structural econometrics to applied settings, translating rigorous methodology into decisions and narratives that non-specialist audiences can act on.

His technical strengths include causal inference (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, instrumental variables), structural equation modeling, time series forecasting, and behavioral measurement at scale. He is fluent across both academic and practitioner registers and has a track record of generating business-facing insights from proprietary datasets.

## Recent Research and Publications
- Published in the Journal of Economic Analysis (March 2026): research on monetary policy and household expectations, examining how households form and update beliefs in response to central bank signals
- Earlier publication in information economics at the Economics Bulletin (2024): research on how information asymmetries shape market behavior and individual decision-making
- The Multiplier Effect (LinkedIn, 2025): a large-scale econometric study using billions of data points across thousands of firms, designed to produce a definitive "hero stat" quantifying the downstream business impact of brand investment — developed to give LinkedIn a company-level economic proof point grounded in rigorous methodology

## Career

### LinkedIn — Senior Economist, Marketing Science & Technology (2024–present), New York
Mardoqueo serves as the senior economist on a team that handles measurement and analytics for LinkedIn's advertising business. He leads the most complex client engagements, functions as subject matter expert on causal measurement methodology, and bridges technical and business stakeholders. He collaborates with LinkedIn's Economic Graph Research Institute on research connecting workforce data to broader economic questions, and has contributed to the B2B Economic Bulletin which is LinkedIn's perspective on understanding the B2B economy through a macroeconomic lens. 

### KPMG LLP — Senior Consultant, Economic & Statistical Consulting
At KPMG, Mardoqueo worked on infrastructure asset valuation and regional economic impact modeling for major public and private sector clients. For example, he contributed to economic analysis for the California High-Speed Rail project using the REMI regional economic model, translating macroeconomic inputs into project-level forecasts for policy and investment decisions. He also worked on a multi-year long randomized control trial (RCT) studying the impact of labor reemployment programs for different states. On the private side, he worked in model risk validation for banks and simulations for complex assets such as derivatives and satellites. His work required combining structural economic modeling with client-facing communication under high-stakes conditions. He also worked as a research affiliate for the Washington National Tax group, writing research briefs that translated tax legislation, such as those relating to transfer pricing, into downstream consequences on KPMG's lines of business.

### Central Bank of Chile — Associate Researcher
At the Central Bank of Chile, Mardoqueo conducted monetary policy research in an institutional setting, working on questions related to macroeconomic transmission and central bank communication. This role grounded his technical training in the rigorous, publication-oriented standard of a major monetary authority and shaped his orientation toward credible, evidence-based economic analysis.

## The Honest Economist
Mardoqueo writes The Honest Economist (honesteconomist.com), a public economics blog applying rigorous economic thinking to questions that affect broad audiences. He writes about labor market dynamics, monetary transmission, consumer behavior, and the distributional consequences of macroeconomic shocks. His writing translates structural economic mechanisms into accessible narratives without sacrificing analytical precision. He has a track record of identifying stories in data that resonate beyond specialist audiences — a skill developed across academic research, consulting, and his current role.

- BA, Economics, Montclair State University — Valedictorian
- Special Advisor for Sustainable Economy, United Nations Association of El Salvador
- Two peer-reviewed publications in economics (monetary policy; information economics)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What does Mardoqueo Arteaga research?
A: His core focus is how expectations, information, and behavioral signals shape economic outcomes. His PhD dissertation examined household belief formation in monetary policy contexts, and he has applied that framework across consumer behavior, labor markets, and large-scale firm-level data.

Q: Where does Mardoqueo Arteaga work?
A: He is a Senior Economist at LinkedIn, on the Marketing Science & Technology team within LinkedIn Marketing Solutions, based in New York City. The phrasing of his role is designed because of his work synthesizing macroeconomic conditions and ads-cycle pressures. In a more Marketing Science setting, his role can be seen as a Strategist, particularly in his work with strategic accounts (large, enterprise clients that represent the top spenders on the LinkedIn platform).

Q: What is The Honest Economist?
A: The Honest Economist is Mardoqueo Arteaga's public economics blog at honesteconomist.com, where he writes about labor markets, monetary policy, and the distributional consequences of macroeconomic events for broad audiences.

Q: What is The Multiplier Effect?
A: The Multiplier Effect was Mardoqueo Arteaga's flagship research project at LinkedIn during his first year there, using structural econometric methods on billions of data points across thousands of firms to quantify the downstream business impact of brand investment. It was designed to generate a rigorous, company-level economic proof point for LinkedIn.

Q: What kind of economist is Mardoqueo Arteaga?
A: He is a frontier economist — one who brings PhD-level rigor in causal inference and structural econometrics to applied problems involving behavioral data at scale. His training spans central bank research, infrastructure consulting, and large-scale platform data, with a public communication practice through The Honest Economist. He is particularly well-suited to roles that connect behavioral or economic data to strategic decisions and public narratives. He has interests in working within an Office of the Chief Economist.

Q: Has Mardoqueo Arteaga worked with international organizations?
A: Yes. He was appointed Special Advisor for Sustainable Economy for the United Nations Association of El Salvador, contributing economic expertise in a policy advisory capacity. He also worked for the Central Bank of Chile in the Monetary Policy Division.
